name: diplococcus
draw: Two small round cocci touching side by side as a pair, like a coffee-bean doublet.

name: tetrad-cocci
draw: Four round cocci arranged in a flat square of two by two.

name: streptobacillus
draw: A chain of three or four short rounded rods joined end to end.

name: vibrio-bacterium
draw: A curved comma-shaped rod with a single long wavy flagellum at one end.

name: peritrichous-bacterium
draw: A rod-shaped bacterium with many wavy flagella sprouting all around its outline.

name: bacterial-endospore
draw: A rod-shaped bacterium with a bold oval spore sitting inside at one end.

name: bacterial-capsule
draw: A rod bacterium surrounded by a thick soft halo outline, showing the slime capsule.

name: prokaryotic-cell
draw: A capsule-shaped cell cutaway with a tangled loop of DNA, a small plasmid ring, dotted ribosomes and a tail flagellum.

name: biofilm
draw: A cluster of small rod bacteria embedded in a wavy mound resting on a flat surface line.

name: bacterial-colony
draw: A single round dome colony seen from above with a scalloped irregular edge and a raised center.

name: magnetotactic-bacterium
draw: A curved rod bacterium with a straight line of small squares (magnet crystals) running along its length.

name: bacterial-flagellar-motor
draw: A rotary motor embedded in a two-line membrane: stacked rings at the base, a hook and a long whip filament rising up.

name: gut-microbiome
draw: A looped intestine outline with small rod and round bacteria scattered inside it.

name: caulobacter
draw: A crescent-shaped bacterium with a thin stalk at one end ending in a small holdfast foot.

name: quorum-sensing
draw: Three small rod bacteria in a triangle with tiny signal dots and short wave arcs passing between them.

name: stromatolite
draw: A group of layered dome-shaped rock mounds in shallow water, each dome showing stacked curved bands.

name: winogradsky-column
draw: A tall clear cylinder filled with horizontal bands of mud and water in different shades, capped at the top.

name: bioremediation
draw: A large oil droplet being nibbled by small rod bacteria around its edge, with a sprout leaf beside it.

name: icosahedral-virus
draw: A twenty-sided geometric capsid seen as a hexagon with inner triangle facets and short knobbed fibers at the corners.

name: helical-virus
draw: A straight rigid rod made of stacked ring segments with a thin spiral RNA line running through it.

name: filovirus
draw: A long thread-like virus curled at one end into a shepherd's crook hook, with tiny spikes along its edge.

name: bullet-shaped-virus
draw: A bullet-shaped virus, flat at one end and rounded at the other, with short spikes around the outline.

name: poxvirus
draw: A rounded brick-shaped virus with a dumbbell-shaped core inside and a textured outer coat.

name: retrovirus
draw: A round enveloped virus with short spikes and a cone-shaped capsid inside holding two RNA squiggles.

name: spike-protein
draw: A single mushroom-shaped protein standing on a membrane line, a wide three-lobed head on a slim stalk.

name: prion
draw: A normal coiled protein beside a misfolded clump of stacked flat arrows, joined by a small arrow.

name: viral-replication
draw: A cell outline with one virus entering on one side and several new virus particles budding out of the other side.

name: giardia
draw: A pear-shaped protozoan seen face-on with two round nuclei like eyes and four pairs of trailing flagella.

name: didinium
draw: A barrel-shaped ciliate with two rings of cilia bands and a pointed snout at the top.

name: malaria-parasite
draw: A round red blood cell with a small signet-ring shaped parasite inside it.

name: toxoplasma
draw: A crescent-shaped banana-like cell with a pointed front end and a round nucleus in the middle.

name: trichomonas
draw: A teardrop-shaped cell with four flagella at the front and a wavy undulating membrane along one side.

name: choanoflagellate
draw: An oval cell with a funnel collar of fine lines on top and a single long flagellum rising from its center.

name: testate-amoeba
draw: A dome-shaped shell with a round opening at the bottom and a few blunt pseudopods poking out.

name: suctorian
draw: A round cell perched on a thin stalk, with many straight tentacles each ending in a small knob.

name: pennate-diatom
draw: A long narrow boat-shaped diatom with a central line and rows of fine stripe marks along both sides.

name: chlorella
draw: A cluster of three or four tiny round green-alga cells, each with a cup-shaped chloroplast inside.

name: pediastrum
draw: A flat star-shaped colony of cells in concentric rings, with twin-horned cells around the edge.

name: scenedesmus
draw: Four bean-shaped cells lined up side by side, the two end cells each with long curved spines.

name: closterium
draw: A slender crescent moon-shaped cell with a small nucleus in the middle and a dot at each tip.

name: micrasterias
draw: A flat symmetric disc cell deeply cut into many lobes, like a snowflake divided in half by a waist.

name: red-algae
draw: A branching feathery seaweed frond with finely divided flat branches.

name: bladderwrack
draw: A forked flat seaweed frond with a midrib and paired round air bladders along it.

name: hydrodictyon
draw: A net-like mesh of cells forming hexagonal openings, like a small fishing net.

name: stonewort
draw: An upright alga stem with whorls of straight thin branches spaced along it like a bottle brush.

name: candida-yeast
draw: A chain of elongated yeast cells forming a branching pseudohypha with round buds at the joints.

name: ascus
draw: A long sac shaped like a narrow pod holding eight round spores in a single row.

name: basidium
draw: A club-shaped cell with four small prongs on top, each bearing a round spore.

name: zygospore
draw: A dark round spiky-walled spore sitting between two short hyphae joining from each side.

name: chytrid-fungus
draw: A round spore body with thin root-like threads below and a single tail flagellum.

name: mycorrhiza
draw: A root tip wrapped in a web of fine fungal threads that spread out into the soil.

name: powdery-mildew
draw: A leaf covered with white powdery patches of fuzzy dots.

name: cell-nucleus
draw: A round nucleus with a double outline dotted with pores and a solid round nucleolus inside.

name: endoplasmic-reticulum
draw: Stacked, folded ribbon-like membrane layers wrapping around one side, studded with tiny ribosome dots.

name: lysosome
draw: A round membrane sac holding scattered small dots and tiny scissors-like enzyme marks.

name: peroxisome
draw: A round membrane sac with a small square crystal core in the center.

name: centriole
draw: Two short barrel cylinders set at right angles to each other, each showing ribbed walls.

name: cytoskeleton
draw: A round cell outline filled with a web of crossing straight and wavy filament lines radiating from the center.

name: microtubule
draw: A hollow cylinder built of rows of small beads in a spiral, shown with one open end.

name: actin-filament
draw: Two twisted strings of round beads winding around each other in a thin rope.

name: cilia
draw: A row of cells along a flat surface, each with many short hairs on top bending in a wave.

name: motor-protein
draw: A two-legged protein walking along a straight bead track while carrying a round vesicle on its back.

name: vesicle-transport
draw: A small round vesicle budding off a membrane with an arrow pointing toward another membrane.

name: exocytosis
draw: A round vesicle fused into a membrane line, opening outward and releasing small dots.

name: apoptosis
draw: A round cell breaking apart into several smaller round blebs with a crack across it.

name: dendritic-cell
draw: A cell body with many long branching arms spreading out in all directions like a star.

name: t-cell
draw: A round lymphocyte with a large nucleus and short Y-shaped receptors dotted around its surface.

name: mast-cell
draw: An oval cell packed with many round granules, a few granules bursting out of one side.

name: fat-cell
draw: A large round cell filled by one big droplet, with a small flattened nucleus pressed against the edge.

name: goblet-cell
draw: A wine-goblet shaped cell with a wide top full of mucus droplets and a narrow stem holding the nucleus.

name: epithelial-tissue
draw: A row of tall column-shaped cells standing side by side, each with an oval nucleus near the base.

name: rod-and-cone-cells
draw: Two slim upright photoreceptor cells side by side, one topped by a long rod and the other by a short cone.

name: myelinated-axon
draw: A long nerve fiber wrapped in a row of sausage-shaped sheath segments with small gaps between them.

name: sarcomere
draw: A striped muscle unit between two zigzag Z lines, with overlapping thick and thin filament bars.

name: root-hair-cell
draw: A long rectangular plant cell with a single long finger-like extension growing out of one side.

name: xylem-vessel
draw: A vertical tube with ring or spiral thickening lines along its walls, stacked from open-ended cells.

name: plasmolysis
draw: A rectangular plant cell wall with the shrunken inner membrane pulled away into a small rounded blob.

name: gap-junction
draw: Two membrane bands side by side joined by short paired tube channels running between them.

name: mitotic-spindle
draw: A lemon-shaped set of fiber lines stretching between two pole dots, with X-shaped chromosomes lined up in the middle.

name: endosymbiosis
draw: A large cell engulfing a smaller oval organelle-like cell, with a curved arrow showing it moving inside.
